117
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, the December 20, 2005/Agrahayana 29, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Civil Aviation; Company Affairs; Finance; Heavy Industries and
Public Enterprises; Panchayati Raj; Petroleum and Natural Gas;
Tourism; Water Resources)
Total number of questions — 20
Rise in tourist inflow
*381. DR. KARAN SINGH:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of TOURISM be
pleased to state:
(a) whether tourist inflow for seven
month period ending August, 2005 is up
by 15.6 per cent to 2.37 Million against
2.05 Million in corresponding period last
year;
(b) whether the annual tourist inflow
has been around 2.3 Million till 2003;
(c) whether with the current growth
rate, the tourist inflow is likely to cross 4
Million mark in 2005;
(d) what steps, Government propose
to take, to improve other facilities in India
so that tourist inflow is further improved;
and
(e) what concrete steps Government
propose to take to provide security
to foreign tourists and also hotel and
other facilities in various parts of the
country?
New irrigation projects
*382. SHRI T.S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of WATER RESOURCES be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
start any new irrigation projects to provide
irrigation facilities to farmers;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether  Government  have
announced any package for the farmers of
Jammu and Kashmir;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) by when this package is likely to be
given?
New opium policy
†*383. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of FINANCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have brought
into force a new rule of moisture in its new
opium policy, if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether as a result of this policy
the small farmers engaged in the cultivation

of opium would suffer losses as they would
be deprived of lease of land; if so, the
number of farmers of the country who
would suffer losses due to this policy of
Government alongwith the State-wise
details thereof;
(c) whether Government would benefit
as a result of this new opium policy; and
(d) if so, the details thereof; and if not,
the reasons for formulation of this policy?
Check on influx of Afghani heroin
*384. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the recent seizures of
narcotics, especially heroin by the
Directorate of Revenue Intelligence
personnel in Delhi indicate that the
contraband originating from Afghanistan is
conduited to world markets via Delhi;
(b) whether the majority of offenders
nabbed by the DRI are from Ghana, Nigeria
and other African nations; and
(c) what steps are being taken to check
the influx of Afghani heroin into the country
for onward carriage?
Acquisition of new planes for Air India
and Indian Airlines
*385. SHRI SHARAD YADAV:
PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL  AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have finally decided to buy new planes for
Air India/Indian Airlines;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the names
of companies which have been short listed
for acquisition of planes for both the
airlines;
(c) by when the orders would be placed
with the manufacturing companies and
planes delivered to the airlines; and
(d) what is the total amount of
expenditure involved in these deals and the
present status of the same?
Loans to SSIs and agricultural
sectors by public sector banks
†*386. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) the measures taken by Government
to provide loans to small scale industries
and agricultural sectors through public
sector banks at cheap rate of interest;
(b) what is the percentage of rate of
interest at which loans to these sectors are
provided currently;
(c) what are the terms and conditions
and time limit for loans without security;
and
(d) details of loans sanctioned to small
scale industrial units by banks during the
past three years, State-wise?
Autonomy to PSUs
*387. SHRI PRAMOD MAHAJAN:
Will the Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES
AND PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
grant more autonomy to some Public Sector
Undertakings;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) the names of such PSUs, which are
likely to be benefited?

Subsidies for Haj
2887. SHRI SK. KHABIR UDDIN
AHMED: Will the Minister of CIVIL
AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
provide subsidies to Haj Pilgrimage for 2005
and 2006 season; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Haj Terminal at Lucknow airport
2888. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a proposal under
consideration of Government to provide
Haj Terminal at Lucknow airport for the
facilities to the Haj pilgrims;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) by when this facility is expected to
be completed?
Infrastructure for air cargo
2889. SHRI KARNENDU
BHATTACHARJEE: Will the Minister of
CIVIL AVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that air-cargo
growth has been significantly higher in the
current financial year;
(b) if so, what is the percentage of
growth;
(c) what steps Government are taking
to sustain the present growth in this sector
in view of competition from the
neighbouring countries including
Bangladesh and Pakistan who are offering
competitive advantage; and
(d) what  steps  Government  are
taking  to  improve  the  infrastructure
to cope up with the increasing number of
flights?

563
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
State Governments' entry in Civil
Aviation sector
2890. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether State Governments are not
allowed to float their own airlines for
operations on international routes;
(b) whether Centre has not allowed
proposal of the State Government of Kerala
to float an airlines to operate flights to Gulf
region;
(c) if so, what are the reasons for same;
(d) how many States have urged Centre
to allow them to float airlines in
international routes; and
(e) whether Government have rejected
all proposals submitted by State
Governments?
Low cost airlines
2891. DR. K. MALAISAMY:
SHRI C. PERUMAL:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) the current status and future
prospects of low cost airlines in the
country;
(b) the number of low cost airlines in
the market;
(c) the reasons for their slow growth
despite of their tremendous potential in
the country, the operational bottlenecks
and regulatory constraints currently faced
by the Civil Aviation sector;
(d) whether low cost carriers in Indian
Aviation industry has not grown
substantially in greater speed and are not
going to stabilize in the coming years; and
(e) what would be their pace of growth?
Direct air service between
Bhubneshwar and Bangalore
2892. MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is no
direct flight between Bhubneshwar and
Bangalore;
(b) whether the State Government has
made a request for this direct flight in view
of development of their IT sector; and
(c) if so, the status of the case and
the time-frame within which it would be
done?
Expansion of international air
services
†2893. PROF. R.B.S. VARMA:
SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY:
Will the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are considering
to increase air services to foreign countries;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the details of air services to America
and Britain at present?

564
Installation of aviation obstruction
warning lights
2894. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
aviation obstruction warning lights which
properly guide the aircrafts are not installed
at the airports in the country;
(b) if so, whether it is a fact that inferior
quality lights are installed at the airports
without proper checking; and
(c) if so, the steps being taken by
Government for proper checking of such
lights for the safety of the aircrafts?
Utilisation of air service agreements
by IA and AI
2895. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA : Will
the Minister of CIVIL AVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of air service agreements
that India have with other countries;
(b) the details of air service agreements
utilised by IA and AI;
(c) whether it is a fact that India is
allowing some of the private airlines to fly
to international destinations; and
(d) if so, the details of private airlines
allowed to fly overseas and details of
destinations to which they are allowed to
fly?
